en: A crab's claw acts as a lever to crush the hard shells of its prey.
Stepping on a wet banana leaf creates very little friction, making it extremely slippery.
Gravity pulls ripe coconuts straight down to the ground when they detach from the tall tree.
Black sand on volcanic beaches contains magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that sticks to magnets.
Combing dry hair with a plastic comb builds up static electricity that attracts small paper bits.
Sunlight refracts and reflects inside spherical raindrops to create a visible rainbow after a rainstorm.
Tree frogs vibrate their vocal sacs to produce loud mating calls that echo through the forest.
Magma deep underground heats groundwater, causing hot water to naturally flow from geothermal springs.
Flowing river water possesses kinetic energy that can erode rocks and turn water turbines.
A woodpecker’s sharp, pointed beak acts as a wedge to pry insects out of tree bark.
A boulder resting at the top of a steep mountain trail has high gravitational potential energy.
A compass needle aligns with Earth’s magnetic field, always pointing toward the magnetic north pole.
